mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals robust economic activity, boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of rising GDPC1 are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the trend reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.1% triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, reflecting market concerns about labor market weakening.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain non-negative despite UNRATE crossing above 4.1%, or the effect dissipates within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS >4.5%) and sustained growth in GDP (GDPC1 >17287) creates a conflicting policy environment, compressing equity valuations and generating negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction does not consistently produce negative returns (e.g., 20-day returns are not significantly lower than baseline in >60% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, sustained increases in federal funds rates above 4.0% lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle, 20-day returns are not significantly negative compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the effect reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in federal funds rates above 4.0% for three consecutive months triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, reflecting prolonged tightening.
failure_condition: The 60-day returns remain non-negative despite FEDFUNDS staying above 4.0% for three months, or the effect diminishes before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE >4.1%) and declining employment growth (PAYEMS <148300) signals labor market stress, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The interaction does not consistently produce negative returns (e.g., 20-day returns are not significantly lower than baseline in >60% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the supply index (INDPRO) signals lower inflationary pressures and stronger growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns in periods of rising INDPRO are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the trend reverses before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in demand measured by HOUST exceeding 1300 units triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days, reflecting immediate consumer spending acceleration.
failure_condition: The 5-day returns do not significantly outperform baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the effect fades within the short horizon.
